finding.claim: SQL injection in ORDER BY: the unvalidated `sort` GET parameter is concatenated into the query. An attacker can inject SQL, for example boolean or time-based blind expressions in a CASE or subquery in ORDER BY, to extract data from any table in the SQLite DB. Stacked queries are generally not possible with PDO sqlite query(), but data exfiltration through blind inference is.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort)

trace.note: concatenated into the SQL string and executed via PDO::query

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, casting, or escaping in list_users_sorted. Compare list_users_safe (line 10-12), which uses an allowlist map, and find_user (line 16-17), which uses a prepared statement. Both are safe. No authentication or authorization checks exist in the file either.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 is accurate and has no allowlist, cast or escaping, since the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in list_users_safe. However, list_users_sorted has no callers in the directory and list.php only defines functions, so I can't confirm that an HTTP request ever reaches it.

verdict_facts.reason: list.php:5-6 takes $_GET['sort'] and concatenates it unvalidated into the ORDER BY clause of a PDO query, and the allowlist at list.php:10-11 is only in the separate list_users_safe function, so list_users_sorted has no guard and an anonymous HTTP client can reach it.
